easy.def: One of the flat parts of something, not the top or bottom.
examples: A box has four sides.
The side of the barn is red.
Write on this side.

more.def: A flat or outer part of something, apart from the top and the bottom.
examples: A square has four sides that are all the same length.
We painted the side of the barn red.
Write your name on the back side of the page.

easy.def: The left or right part of something.
examples: Sit on this side.
The park is on the other side.
Stand by my side.

more.def: One of the two halves or areas of a place, as divided by a line.
examples: The bridge crosses to the other side of the river.
Cars drive on the right side of the road.
She sat by his side during the movie.
The house was silent at night.
The class was silent for the test.
Snow makes the world silent.
The forest was silent after the snowfall.
The crowd fell silent when the music began.
She stayed silent because she did not know the answer.
Our shoes are similar. They are both blue.
The two cats look similar.
A lemon is similar to a lime.

more.def: Alike in many ways, but not exactly the same.
examples: A wolf looks similar to a large dog.
Their voices are so similar that I mix them up on the phone.
The two towns have similar weather.
This puzzle is simple.
The game has simple rules.
I made a simple lunch.

more.def: Easy to understand or do; not hard or complicated.
examples: The directions were simple, so we finished quickly.
She wore a simple blue dress.
There is a simple way to fix the problem.

easy.def: From a time in the past until now.
examples: I have been here since noon.
She has been sick since Monday.
We played since lunch.

more.def: From a certain time in the past up to now.
examples: I have lived in this town since I was a baby.
It has rained since early this morning.
He has been reading since breakfast.

easy.def: A word used to give a reason.
examples: Since it is cold, wear a coat.
I stayed in since I was sick.
Since you are here, help me.

more.def: A word used to give the reason for something.
examples: Since it was raining, we ate lunch indoors.
I took an umbrella since the sky looked dark.
Since you know the way, you can lead us.

easy.def: A polite word used to speak to a man.
examples: Yes, sir.
Excuse me, sir.
Thank you, sir.

more.def: A polite word used when speaking to a man, especially one you do not know or one who is older.
examples: Excuse me, sir, you dropped your hat.
Yes, sir, I will be there at noon.
Can I help you carry that, sir?

easy.def: A girl who has the same parents as you.
examples: My sister is tall.
I play with my sister.
Her sister is six.

more.def: A girl or woman who has the same parents as another person.
examples: My older sister helps me with my reading.
He has two sisters, and they love to bake.
Her little sister follows her around the yard.

easy.def: To rest with your bottom on a seat or the ground.
examples: Sit on the chair.
The cat sat on my lap.
We sit in a circle.

more.def: To rest with your weight on your bottom, rather than on your feet.
examples: Please sit quietly on the rug while I read.
The birds sat on the wire, side by side.
We sat around the campfire and sang songs.
